navigation.title: Navigation and Shell Chrome
navigation.purpose: Global chrome surrounding every NusaShell view: title bar, sidebar, connection status, and storage indicator.
navigation.howToOpen: Always visible when the NusaShell window is open.

sections.heading: Title bar
paragraphs: Identifies NusaShell with its brand mark and wordmark, followed by compact backend connection status, a mini-window shortcut, an install shortcut (visible only while the browser offers installation), and a settings shortcut.

sections.heading: Sidebar
paragraphs: Vertical navigation on the left, ordered Home, Agent, Skills, Learning, Automation, Plugins, Providers, and Logs. It can show icons with labels or icons only, and remembers that choice locally. Below 680px viewport width the sidebar becomes an off-canvas drawer: the title-bar hamburger toggles it open, and it closes on backdrop click, Escape, or selecting a nav item.
Keyboard: Ctrl/Cmd+K or / focuses the search box on the current view. Escape dismisses dialogs, toasts stay on hover, and Ctrl/Cmd+N starts a new agent conversation when the Agent view is open.

sections.heading: Offline screen
paragraphs: Full-window overlay shown whenever the backend is unreachable. It covers every view so no half-broken UI stays interactive: an explicit offline verdict shows it immediately, while closed/error/reconnecting states only cover after a short persistence window so quick reconnects never flicker. Recovery hides it instantly and Try again reloads the shell (service worker serves the cached shell while the server is down).

home.title: Home
home.purpose: The launcher view: a grid of installed plugin apps. Each tile opens the plugin UI in a separate browser window. Searchable by name, id, or description and filterable by category.
home.howToOpen: Open NusaShell, or click the Home item in the left sidebar.

sections.heading: Filter row
paragraphs: A search input filters the app grid by name, id, or description. Category tabs narrow the grid to a single category. Escape or the clear button resets the search.

sections.heading: App grid
paragraphs: A responsive grid of plugin tiles. Each tile shows the plugin icon, name, and a runtime status when active. Clicking a tile opens the plugin UI in a new browser window sized from the plugin manifest.

agent.title: Agent
agent.purpose: The default view: multi-conversation chat against any configured provider model. Each conversation keeps its own history on disk and can use skills, memory, docs, plugin-provided MCP tools, and spawned ACP subagents.
agent.howToOpen: Open NusaShell, or click the Agent item in the left sidebar.

sections.heading: Conversations pane
paragraphs: Lists conversations with a search filter and a New conversation button. The count reflects persisted threads. On narrow widths the pane hides behind a Rooms button and a backdrop; Escape or choosing a room closes it. Ctrl/Cmd+K focuses this search; Ctrl/Cmd+N creates a thread.

sections.heading: Thread
paragraphs: Renders the active conversation. An empty thread offers starter prompt chips that fill the composer.

Long conversations open showing only the most recent messages, scrolled to the bottom. A 'Load older messages' button at the top reveals earlier in-memory messages (including older rounds of a finished assistant turn), then archived pre-compaction chunks, one batch at a time. Chunks are never auto-loaded after a turn finishes or mid-turn compaction. Snapshot render keeps the immediate user or compaction bubble and a short tail of a finished turn. A running turn keeps every persisted round of that turn mounted on open and reload — Load older still reveals earlier complete turns and archived chunks. Live streaming coalesces delta rendering per animation frame. Thinking is parsed when the disclosure is opened. Live streaming auto-follows only while the view is pinned to the bottom.

sections.heading: Tool call strip
paragraphs: Shows in-flight tool calls for the current turn, with one entry per MCP or built-in tool invocation.

Streaming tools (exec) display their live output as it is produced and offer a per-call Stop button while running; the button cancels the underlying turn via agent.turns.stop (same as the composer Stop).

sections.heading: ACP subagent dock
paragraphs: Appears above the composer when ACP subagents are live (or recently finished in this room). Each chip opens the right-hand drawer; the peek control opens a popup for one run. Drawer and popup support steer, stop, mode changes, and risk promotion. Permission prompts use a global overlay that stays visible across views.

sections.heading: ACP live views
paragraphs: The drawer lists every live spawn so you can switch between parallel subagents. The peek popup focuses one run. The permission overlay is fail-closed: timeout denies. Allow once, allow for this session, or deny.

sections.heading: Task checklist
paragraphs: A compact strip showing the agent's todo list for the current conversation. Items come from the `todo` tool; the user can delete items from the UI.

sections.heading: Steer queue
paragraphs: When a user sends a steer message mid-turn, it is queued here and applied at the next safe tool-round boundary.

sections.heading: Composer
paragraphs: The message input with attachments, model picker, workspace selector, provider status, stop, and send buttons. Ctrl+Enter (⌘↩ on Mac) sends. While a turn is running, Send becomes Steer. The whole conversation area accepts drag & drop of files and folders — folders are attached as path-only references (desktop only).

skills.title: Skills
skills.purpose: Browse and read installed skill packages (SKILL.md + support files). Skills come from three owners: user, builtin, and plugin:<id>. Lower-priority owners (plugin) are shadowed when a higher-priority owner (user/builtin) defines the same skill ID.
skills.howToOpen: Click the Skills item in the left sidebar.

sections.heading: Header
paragraphs: View title and a New skill button.

sections.heading: Catalog
paragraphs: Searchable list of installed skills. Each row shows the skill name, an owner badge (user/builtin/plugin:<id>), and last-updated time. Shadowed skills are dimmed. The count reflects persisted skills.

sections.heading: Detail
paragraphs: Read-only viewer for the selected skill. Shows the skill name, description, and owner, plus a file tree (SKILL.md + support files) on the left and the selected file's content on the right. Plugin-owned skills are read-only.

plugins.title: Plugins
plugins.purpose: Manage all plugins: manual MCP servers, MCP-only plugins, and MCP + UI plugins appear in one catalog.
plugins.howToOpen: Click the Plugins item in the left sidebar.

sections.heading: Header
paragraphs: View title and two buttons: Add MCP opens the MCP server editor (stdio child process, SSE, or Streamable HTTP remote endpoint); Install plugin opens the plugin installer with catalog, GitHub, and ZIP options.

sections.heading: Plugin installer
paragraphs: A tabbed dialog for installing plugins. Catalog shows official first-party plugins. GitHub installs from a repository URL, optionally targeting a subdirectory for monorepos. Upload ZIP lets the user browse or drop a plugin archive.

sections.heading: Plugin window
paragraphs: Plugin UIs open in a separate browser window served same-origin at /plugins/<id>/ (the server injects the window.shell shim). Opening happens from Home tiles and the Plugins drawer Open UI button. The window is sized from the manifest ui.window (panel/widget request defaultSize with a 700x700 / 380x280 fallback; fullscreen opens a normal browser window). This keeps the plugin from covering or replacing the NusaShell UI. If the browser blocks the pop-up, a toast prompts the user to allow pop-ups.

sections.heading: Plugin catalog
paragraphs: Lists all plugins — manual MCP servers, MCP-only plugins, and MCP + UI plugins — with runtime state (idle/connected). Clicking a row opens the Plugins detail drawer.

sections.heading: Detail drawer
paragraphs: A right-hand drawer that opens when a catalog row is clicked. Shows the state machine, actions, preferences, tools, and manifest summary. Native MCP rows expose Start, Stop, Restart, Edit, and Delete; plugin rows expose Start, Stop, Restart, and Uninstall; MCP + UI plugins also expose Open UI. When a catalog plugin has a newer release, an Update button appears that updates it in place (plugin.update). Close with the X button, overlay, or Escape. The manifest summary shows transport plus URL for SSE/HTTP servers, or command plus arguments for stdio servers. The same editor (opened via Add MCP or Edit) switches its fields per transport: command/args/env for stdio, URL/headers for SSE/HTTP.

The Preferences area has an Auto start switch (shown for every entry) that launches the MCP server when NusaShell starts, and an Auto update switch (shown only for catalog-managed plugins) that updates the plugin automatically when a new version is released.

providers.title: Providers
providers.purpose: Configure persistent Anthropic, OpenAI, and OpenRouter cards, add unlimited custom OpenRouter-compatible providers by wire format (Messages, Responses, Chat), and manage spawn-only ACP subagent binaries. Chat API keys live in the local SQLite credential store. ACP env values stay on disk in acp-agents.json; the wire API only returns env keys.
providers.howToOpen: Click the Providers item in the left sidebar.

sections.heading: Header
paragraphs: View title plus Add custom provider (unlimited OpenRouter-compatible gateways) and Add ACP agent (spawn-only subprocesses).

sections.heading: Chat providers
paragraphs: The registry always shows persistent Anthropic, OpenAI, and OpenRouter cards, even before configuration. Anthropic uses the Anthropic Messages driver; OpenAI uses the OpenAI Responses driver; OpenRouter and custom providers use the OpenRouter driver. OpenRouter and custom forms expose Messages, Responses, and Chat API kinds. Selecting a card opens the detail pane for editing its base URL, API key, enabled state, importing models, and testing connectivity. These models appear in the Agent composer.

sections.heading: ACP subagents
paragraphs: A separate registry for Agent Client Protocol binaries. Register a generic command + args + env. Probe discovers auth methods, modes, and models at runtime. ACP agents never appear in the composer; the parent agent spawns them with the subagent tool. Command is immutable after save.

learning.title: Learning
learning.purpose: Search accumulated memory entries and skills via hybrid BM25 + embedding + graph search, explore how they connect in the knowledge graph, and review what autolearn saved.
learning.howToOpen: Click the Learning item in the left sidebar.

sections.heading: Header stats
paragraphs: Live counts of memory entries and learning edges. The memory count refreshes in real time when a tool or the background review agent saves, promotes, or demotes a memory entry (via the `memory.updated` event).

sections.heading: Tabs
paragraphs: Switches between Memory & Graph (search + graph) and Learning log (autolearn activity feed). The log loads lazily on first open.

sections.heading: Search bar
paragraphs: Hybrid search across memory and skills, with a kind filter (All, Skills, Memory) and a Search button.

sections.heading: Results
paragraphs: Ranked search results with a count. With an empty query the pane lists all skills and memories so content is visible immediately. Memory entries show a tier badge (primary or fragment) next to the kind label so the two tiers are visually distinguishable. Memory entries have a delete button (×) that opens a confirm dialog and calls memory.delete. Long content is collapsed to 3 lines; click to expand. Results refresh automatically when memory or skills change (via `memory.updated` / `skill.updated` events, debounced 300ms).

sections.heading: Splitter
paragraphs: Draggable splitter between the results pane and the graph pane. Drag to resize the results pane width; the width persists to localStorage.

sections.heading: Knowledge graph
paragraphs: Force-directed graph (vis-network) of skills, memory entries, and their edges. Refresh reloads the graph; Fit fits it to view. Legend distinguishes Skill, Memory, Related, and Used-with edges. The graph refreshes automatically when memory or skills change (via `memory.updated` / `skill.updated` events, debounced 300ms).

sections.heading: Learning log
paragraphs: Autolearn activity feed from the trajectory log (review runs, extraction, edge building, consolidation, decay, prune), newest first. Review entries show a status badge (done or error) with the error message when failed, a compact Source <title> line (raw conversation id hidden), the saved outcomes (kind + snippet) or an explicit Nothing to save. line, per-type extras, and a View review details button. Expanding it replays what the background review agent did exactly like an Agent-view conversation - Thinking disclosures per round, terminal-style tool cards with input/output panels, short narration notes, and the final verdict - but never the replayed user transcript. A running indicator appears at the top while a review is in-flight. Refresh reloads the feed.

automation.title: Automation
automation.purpose: Manage durable once/every/when automations, inspect DAG runs, and see waiting or blocked states without occupying a runner.
automation.howToOpen: Click the Automation item in the left sidebar.

sections.heading: Header stats
paragraphs: Counts of runnable, blocked, and waiting automations so provider outages are visible without opening a run.

sections.heading: Toolbar
paragraphs: Tabs switch between Workflows, Runs, Schedules, and Events. New automation opens a once/every/when/manual wizard. Pipeline files from the data directory appear alongside saved automations in the Workflows tab.

sections.heading: Blocked provider
paragraphs: When a saved automation depends on a disabled MCP provider it stays BLOCKED rather than FAILED. Enable provider restores the binding without rewriting the workflow.

sections.heading: List and detail
paragraphs: The list shows the active tab. The detail pane renders job needs as a DAG, waiting wake times, and run/enable/disable/cancel actions.

logs.title: Logs
logs.purpose: Runtime events streamed live from the shell via WebSocket. The log file is a bounded ring (2000 entries) persisted as JSONL.
logs.howToOpen: Click the Logs item in the left sidebar.

sections.heading: Filters
paragraphs: Level filter (All/debug/info/warn/error), entry count, Follow toggle, and Clear button.

sections.heading: Tail
paragraphs: Scrolling list of log entries. When Follow is on, the tail auto-scrolls to the newest entry.

settings.title: Settings
settings.purpose: Control how this local NusaShell instance runs agent turns, manages context, picks embedding models, and presents the workspace. Browser-only preferences stay in local storage.
settings.howToOpen: Click the settings icon in the title bar, or press the Settings shortcut.

sections.heading: Header
paragraphs: View title and a Save settings button with a live status indicator.

sections.heading: Agent runtime
paragraphs: Default model for new conversations, the maximum tool rounds per turn (default 8), the max parallel tools per round (default 6, range 1–64), and the plugin usage-contract enforcement mode. Existing conversations keep their selected model.

sections.heading: Embeddings
paragraphs: Embedding model used by skill and memory search. Models tagged as embedding-capable appear here after import. The learning review threshold controls how many turns accumulate before extracting learnings (default 10, 0 disables turn-based review). The review model routes background autolearn reviews to a cheaper or faster model (default uses the conversation's active model). Project memory directory overrides the default {dataDir}/memory_project store so a skill-compatible path such as ~/.memory can be shared with other agents.

sections.heading: Vision fallback
paragraphs: When the active chat model cannot see images, NusaShell can describe attached images using a separate vision-capable model so the conversation continues without errors. Pick any model that supports image input. Leave disabled if you always use vision-capable chat models.

sections.heading: Image generation
paragraphs: Pick the model used by the generate_image tool. This is separate from the chat model — any chat model can orchestrate, and the image backend is resolved here. OpenAI Images and OpenRouter Image API are supported. Import models on an OpenAI or OpenRouter provider. Leave disabled until you want the agent to be able to generate images.

sections.heading: Audio fallback
paragraphs: When the active chat model cannot hear audio, NusaShell can transcribe or describe attached audio files using a separate audio-capable model so the conversation continues without errors. Pick any model that supports audio input. Leave disabled if you always use audio-capable chat models.

sections.heading: Speech generation
paragraphs: Pick the model used by the generate_speech tool (text-to-speech). Online models use an OpenAI-compatible /audio/speech endpoint. The offline piper engine can be installed with one click: the install button opens a dialog with a voice picker (Bahasa Indonesia news_tts medium, English US lessac high), downloads the piper binary plus the selected voice model into the data directory with live progress, and the installed voice then appears as an option in the model picker (provider “piper”) so it can be selected directly — the automatic fallback works as soon as install finishes, no offline-mode checkbox needed. The old manual checkbox stays for PIPER_BIN/PATH setups.

sections.heading: Offline speech-to-text
paragraphs: Lets read_media transcribe audio locally with whisper.cpp (whisper-cli) — no API key, no network. The engine binary is downloaded once during install; models land under models/stt/ in the data directory. The install button opens a requirements dialog: a checklist (platform support, whisper.cpp engine, GGML model, free disk), a per-OS guide (Linux/Windows auto-install from official releases, macOS via brew install whisper-cpp), a model picker over the multilingual catalog (tiny/base/small-q5_1/small default/large-v3-turbo variants; Indonesian and English supported; .en variants excluded), and live download progress with speed. After install the model appears in the Offline STT model select and read_media uses it automatically.

sections.heading: Video fallback
paragraphs: When the active chat model cannot see video, NusaShell can describe attached video files using a separate video-capable model so the conversation continues without errors. Pick any model that supports video input. Leave disabled if you always use video-capable chat models.

sections.heading: Context compaction
paragraphs: Toggle compaction, set max input tokens (fallback context window, default 200000), max output tokens (default 65536), pick an optional compaction model (default uses the active chat model), prompt caching, and optional sampling parameters (temperature, top-p, top-k, frequency penalty, presence penalty).

sections.heading: Appearance
paragraphs: Browser-only preferences stored locally, not sent to the agent.

sections.heading: Connection
paragraphs: Backend status, automatic reconnect toggle, and a Check connection button. The Go shell uses HTTP RPC for commands and WebSocket for live events.

sections.heading: System
paragraphs: Local diagnostics: version, data directory, and transports. This browser version does not manage desktop tray or login startup.

telemetry.title: Telemetry
telemetry.purpose: Aggregate token usage, spend, and caching across all conversations. Mirrors the OpenRouter Activity dashboard layout with summary metric cards and time-series charts.
telemetry.howToOpen: Click the Telemetry item in the left sidebar.

sections.heading: Header
paragraphs: Range selector (15m / 30m / 1h / 3h default / 1d / 2d / 1w / 1mo / 1y / All) and Refresh button.

sections.heading: Summary metrics
paragraphs: Four metric cards: Total spend (USD), Requests, Total tokens, Cache hit percent.

sections.heading: Usage by model
paragraphs: Stacked bar chart showing daily spend broken down by model.

sections.heading: Top models
paragraphs: Ranked table of models by spend, with request and token counts.

sections.heading: Token breakdown
paragraphs: Stacked bar chart showing daily prompt, completion, and cache-read tokens.

sections.heading: Prompt token caching
paragraphs: Stacked bar chart showing daily cached vs uncached prompt tokens.

sections.heading: Request volume by model
paragraphs: Stacked bar chart showing daily request counts broken down by model.

sections.heading: Top providers
paragraphs: Ranked table of providers by spend, with request and token counts.

sidebar.label: Sidebar
sidebar.notes: Holds navigation items and storage indicator.

search-input.label: App search
search-input.action: Filters installed apps by name, id, or description. Escape clears the query.

search-clear.label: Clear app search
search-clear.action: Clears the app search and returns focus to the search input.

launcher-tabs.label: App categories
launcher-tabs.action: Filters the app grid to a category.

app-grid.label: App grid
app-grid.action: Click an app tile to open its plugin UI in a separate browser window.

new-conversation-btn.label: New conversation
new-conversation-btn.action: Creates a new conversation and focuses the composer.

conversation-search.label: Conversation search
conversation-search.notes: Filters conversation titles in real time.

agent-rooms-toggle.label: Rooms
agent-rooms-toggle.action: On narrow widths, opens the conversations pane as a drawer. Escape or the backdrop closes it.

agent-rooms-backdrop.label: Rooms backdrop
agent-rooms-backdrop.action: Click to close the conversations drawer.

agent-thread.label: Thread log
agent-thread.notes: Renders the active conversation messages. Long conversations are windowed: the last user bubble plus a short tail of a finished turn render on open (scrolled to bottom). A running turn keeps every persisted round of that turn mounted on reload. Older finished-turn rounds, earlier turns, and archived chunks load on demand via Load older or scroll-to-top. Thinking markdown is parsed when expanded. An empty thread shows starter prompt chips.

agent-starter-prompts.label: Starter prompts
agent-starter-prompts.action: Fills the composer with a ready-to-edit prompt. Available on an empty thread.

agent-load-older.label: Load older messages
agent-load-older.action: Reveals the previous batch of older in-memory messages (first older rounds of a finished turn, then earlier turns), then archived pre-compaction chunks, keeping the scroll position anchored. Shown while older messages or unloaded chunks remain; hidden once the oldest history is reached. A running turn already mounts its full persisted round list, so this button is for earlier complete turns and archives.

agent-composer-stack.label: Composer stack
agent-composer-stack.notes: Holds ACP dock, tool strip, todo strip, steer queue, and composer.

tool-job-strip.label: Tool calls strip
tool-job-strip.notes: In-flight tool calls for the current turn.

agent-todo-strip-list.label: Task list
agent-todo-strip-list.notes: Items come from the `todo` tool; user-deleted items disappear.

agent-steer-queue.label: Steer queue
agent-steer-queue.notes: Queued steer messages waiting for a safe boundary.

composer-input.label: Message input
composer-input.shortcut: Ctrl+Enter / ⌘↩ to send; Escape closes dialogs

agent-file-input.label: File input
agent-file-input.notes: Hidden file picker for images, PDFs, and text files.

model-menu.label: Model menu
model-menu.notes: Lists models grouped by provider with effort chips.

agent-provider-status.label: Provider status / context usage
agent-provider-status.notes: Shows the backend context usage as used/window (e.g. 32k/1M). The number is the server source of truth: the live server-side estimate while a turn streams and the provider-measured context fill after it completes. The frontend never sums message bubbles.

stop-btn.label: Stop
stop-btn.action: Cancels the running turn; partial output is kept and marked interrupted.

skill-editor-title.label: Editor title
skill-editor-title.notes: Shows the selected skill name or 'No file selected'.

skill-editor-empty.label: Editor empty state
skill-editor-empty.notes: Empty state shown when no file is selected. Prompts user to pick a file from the skill tree.

plugins-add-mcp.label: Add MCP
plugins-add-mcp.action: Opens the native MCP server editor.

plugin-table.label: Plugin catalog
plugin-table.notes: Lists all plugins with runtime status and tool chips. Clicking a row opens the Plugins detail drawer.

plugin-drawer.label: Plugin detail drawer
plugin-drawer.notes: Right-hand panel showing state machine, actions, tools, and manifest for the selected catalog item.

plugin-drawer-overlay.label: Drawer overlay
plugin-drawer-overlay.action: Clicking the overlay closes the drawer.

plugin-state-machine.label: State machine
plugin-state-machine.notes: Shows idle → connecting → connected → error with the current state highlighted.

plugin-btn-open-ui.label: Open UI
plugin-btn-open-ui.action: Opens the selected MCP + UI plugin in a separate browser window (served at /plugins/<id>/). Hidden for MCP-only entries.

plugin-btn-start.label: Start
plugin-btn-start.action: Connects the selected MCP server or plugin and lists its tools.

plugin-btn-restart.label: Restart
plugin-btn-restart.action: Stops then starts the selected MCP server or plugin.

plugin-btn-update.label: Update
plugin-btn-update.action: Updates a catalog plugin in place to its latest release (plugin.update). Appears only when a newer catalog version is available; the label shows the target version.

plugin-btn-edit.label: Edit
plugin-btn-edit.action: Opens the MCP server editor for the selected native MCP entry. Hidden for plugins.

plugin-btn-delete.label: Delete
plugin-btn-delete.action: Deletes the selected manual MCP-server plugin (plugin.delete). Hidden for installed plugins.

plugin-btn-uninstall.label: Uninstall
plugin-btn-uninstall.action: Uninstalls the selected plugin and drops its MCP connection (plugin.uninstall). Hidden for native MCP entries.

plugin-drawer-autostart.label: Auto start section
plugin-drawer-autostart.notes: Preference row shown for every entry; contains the auto-start switch.

plugin-autostart-toggle.label: Auto start
plugin-autostart-toggle.action: Launches this MCP server or plugin automatically when NusaShell starts (plugin.set_autostart).

plugin-drawer-autoupdate.label: Auto update section
plugin-drawer-autoupdate.notes: Preference row shown only for catalog-managed plugins; contains the auto-update switch.

plugin-autoupdate-toggle.label: Auto update
plugin-autoupdate-toggle.action: Updates this catalog plugin automatically when a new version is released (plugin.set_autoupdate). Shown only for catalog-managed plugins.

plugin-tools-list.label: Tools list
plugin-tools-list.notes: Lists the tools exposed by the connected MCP server or plugin with name and description.

plugin-tool-count.label: Tool count
plugin-tool-count.notes: Number of tools currently loaded for the selected entry.

plugin-manifest-info.label: Manifest info
plugin-manifest-info.notes: Key/value summary of the selected MCP server or plugin, including version, category, and install path when available.

add-provider-btn.label: Add custom provider
add-provider-btn.action: Opens the custom OpenRouter-compatible provider editor; users can save any number of custom providers.

provider-registry.label: Provider registry
provider-registry.notes: Always contains Anthropic, OpenAI, and OpenRouter cards, followed by any number of custom provider cards. OpenRouter and custom cards show their selected API kind.

provider-detail.label: Provider detail
provider-detail.notes: Edit form for the selected provider.

learning-graph-refresh.label: Reload graph
learning-graph-refresh.action: Reloads the graph from the backend.

learning-graph-fit.label: Fit to view
learning-graph-fit.action: Fits the graph to the viewport.

learning-tab-memory.label: Memory & Graph tab
learning-tab-memory.notes: Shows the search + knowledge graph panel.

learning-log.label: Learning log
learning-log.notes: Trajectory events; review entries have done/error/skipped status badges. Skipped entries explain whether a trigger was coalesced because another review was running or deferred by retry cooldown. Completed review entries have a View review details button that expands the background review agent's activity digest inline.

settings-max-parallel-tools.label: Max parallel tools
settings-max-parallel-tools.notes: 1–64, default 6. Bounds concurrent tool calls per assistant round.

settings-learning-threshold.label: Learning review threshold
settings-learning-threshold.notes: Turns before review; 0 disables turn-based review.

settings-skill-nudge-interval.label: Skill review threshold
settings-skill-nudge-interval.notes: Tool calls before skill review; 0 disables tool-based review.

settings-project-memory-base.label: Project memory directory
settings-project-memory-base.notes: Absolute directory for {key}/{kind}.md project memory. Empty uses {dataDir}/memory_project. ~/.memory shares the skill-compatible layout.

settings-review-model.label: Review model
settings-review-model.notes: Routes background autolearn reviews to a dedicated model; empty uses the conversation's active model.

settings-compaction-model.label: Compaction model
settings-compaction-model.notes: Route compaction summarization to a cheaper or faster model. Default uses the conversation's active model.

settings-sound-notifications.label: Sound notifications
settings-sound-notifications.notes: Play a sound when an agent turn completes or fails. Default on.

settings-stt-language.label: Audio language
settings-stt-language.notes: Offline STT language: auto-detect, Bahasa Indonesia, or English.

plugin-install-cancel.label: Cancel install
plugin-install-cancel.action: Closes the plugin installer without installing.

plugin-install-confirm.label: Confirm install
plugin-install-confirm.action: Confirms the current install source (GitHub or ZIP).

plugin-install-error.label: Install error banner
plugin-install-error.notes: Inline error shown inside the installer when an install attempt fails; cleared on tab switch or dialog close.

plugin-catalog-search.label: Plugin catalog search
plugin-catalog-search.action: Filters the plugin catalog by name, id, or description.

add-acp-agent-btn.label: Add ACP agent
add-acp-agent-btn.action: Opens a generic command/args/env form to register a spawn-only ACP binary.

acp-agent-registry.label: ACP agent registry
acp-agent-registry.notes: Cards for spawn-only ACP binaries. Not shown in the Agent composer.

acp-agent-detail.label: ACP agent detail
acp-agent-detail.notes: Edit label/args/env, probe, authenticate, refresh catalog, and map advertised modes to risk tiers. Command is read-only after save.

acp-dock.label: ACP subagent dock
acp-dock.notes: Hidden until at least one live or recently finished ACP run exists.

acp-drawer-overlay.label: ACP drawer overlay
acp-drawer-overlay.action: Click to close the subagent drawer.

acp-drawer.label: ACP subagent drawer
acp-drawer.notes: Wider than the plugin drawer so a live transcript, steer box, and mode chips fit.

acp-popup-overlay.label: ACP peek overlay
acp-popup-overlay.action: Click outside the dialog to close the peek popup.

tm-spend.label: Total spend metric
tm-spend.notes: Aggregate USD spend for the selected period.

tm-requests.label: Total requests metric
tm-requests.notes: Total assistant turns with usage data.

tm-tokens.label: Total tokens metric
tm-tokens.notes: Sum of input + output + cache tokens.

chart-usage-model.label: Usage by model chart
chart-usage-model.notes: Stacked bar chart of daily spend per model.

tm-top-models.label: Top models table
tm-top-models.notes: Ranked list of models by spend.

chart-token-breakdown.label: Token breakdown chart
chart-token-breakdown.notes: Stacked bar chart of daily prompt/completion/cache tokens.

chart-caching.label: Prompt caching chart
chart-caching.notes: Stacked bar chart of cached vs uncached prompt tokens.

chart-requests.label: Request volume chart
chart-requests.notes: Stacked bar chart of daily requests per model.

tm-top-providers.label: Top providers table
tm-top-providers.notes: Ranked list of providers by spend.

skill-tree-meta.label: Skill tree meta
skill-tree-meta.notes: Shows skill name or 'No skill selected' in the tree pane header.

skill-tree-empty.label: Skill tree empty state
skill-tree-empty.notes: Empty state shown when no skill is selected or skill has no files.

skill-file-viewer.label: Skill file viewer
skill-file-viewer.notes: Shows file content when a file is clicked in the skill tree.

skill-file-path.label: Skill file path
skill-file-path.notes: Path of the currently opened file.

skill-file-size.label: Skill file size
skill-file-size.notes: Size of the currently opened file.

skill-file-content.label: Skill file content
skill-file-content.notes: Pre-formatted text content of the opened skill file.

skills-splitter-1.label: Catalog/tree splitter
skills-splitter-1.notes: Draggable divider between Catalog and Skill tree panes. Persists width to localStorage.

skills-splitter-2.label: Tree/editor splitter
skills-splitter-2.notes: Draggable divider between Skill tree and Editor panes. Persists width to localStorage.

skills-workspace.label: Skills workspace grid
skills-workspace.notes: 3-column grid with CSS variable widths for draggable splitters.

install-skill-btn.label: Install skill button
install-skill-btn.notes: Opens file picker to install a .skill or .zip archive.

skill-file-input.label: Skill file input
skill-file-input.notes: Hidden file input accepting .skill and .zip files for skill installation.

settings-plugin-contract-mode.label: Plugin usage contracts
settings-plugin-contract-mode.notes: How agents are nudged toward a plugin's usage contract (read via contract_read). Empty = factory default (hint, advisory); off never notifies; hint attaches an advisory note until the contract is read; require blocks MCP calls until the contract is read.

offline-screen.label: Offline screen
offline-screen.notes: Full-window overlay covering every view while the backend is unreachable; hidden again the moment the connection reopens.

offline-retry-btn.label: Try again
offline-retry-btn.notes: Reloads the shell; the service worker serves the cached app while the server is down.

mini-window-btn.label: Mini window
mini-window-btn.notes: Opens the picture-in-picture mini window (Document PiP on Chromium, popup fallback elsewhere) showing the live agent thread.

pwa-install-btn.label: Install NusaShell
pwa-install-btn.notes: Visible only while the browser offers installation (beforeinstallprompt); triggers the native install flow and hides after install/dismissal.

tool-terminal-stop.label: Tool terminal stop
tool-terminal-stop.action: Cancels the running turn for this tool call (agent.turns.stop). Shown only on streaming tools (exec) while the tool is running; the button hides once the tool settles.
tool-terminal-stop.notes: Appears inside the tool terminal card's summary row (class agent-tool-stop), next to the elapsed timer.
